valuation.antimatterValue: annihilate(stable, recipient, amount, min) burns `amount` AM, pulls a matching stable deposit, and mints `amount` UNBACKED phUSD (Antimatter itself) plus `amount*exchangeRate` stable-backed phUSD (PhusdStableMinter). At phUSD = p and exchangeRate about 1, 1 AM is worth about 2p - 1. At p = 0.947 that is about $0.89 per AM, before slippage. The only exit is the about $23k-deep phUSD/sUSDS pair, so large realizations are worth less.
valuation.dilutionVsOpportunityCost: Bonfire AM is NOT externally-derived yield. Each AM is a bearer claim on 1 unbacked phUSD, so the memory rule 'externally-derived yield over-payment = opportunity cost' does NOT apply (same carve-out as stable-staker-v2-emits-antimatter-premise-void). Minted AM is real dilution of phUSD holders. It is however the story's stated intent ('Liquidity takes the hit instead, via eventual antimatter annihilation'), and it is owner-BUDGETED: for any sequence of burns, cumulative bonfire mint <= sum of ratePerDay_i x dt_i / 1 day (floored; the cap only ever forfeits). No burner action can raise total emission. Burners only compete over WHO receives a fixed, owner-set stream. Example: at the story's 2.5 AM/day, the cost is about 912.5 unbacked phUSD/yr, about 0.93% of current phUSD supply, about $2.2/day of market value.
valuation.nftCostFloor: Cheapest fresh NFT is about $3.6 (V1 EYE or SCX mint + NFTMigrator.migrate, simulated on the fork; see ECON-003), rising 10% per mint. Cheapest V2-native mint is $10.02 USDC (idx3). The binding floor is the about 772 idle unstaked V2 NFTs plus about 4.6k staked ones, whose marginal cost to a holder is about 0 once SYA gating is retired. So the pot clears near (gas + holder reservation value), well below any fresh-mint cost, at any sane rate.
valuation.priceGrowthExternality: Buying an NFT to burn raises that index's V2 price by growthBasisPoints (1-2bp on live idx1-4; 0 on idx7; 1200bp on idx5). V2 prices never decay, so mint-to-burn demand ratchets the price up for later minters. That is a revenue gain for the protocol (payment goes to dispatchers), not a loss. Mint-to-burn is net-positive for the protocol compared with an idle-inventory burn of the same pot, because the pot is paid either way and the mint adds dispatcher revenue.

findings.title: Lowering maxPayout after the pot has grown is front-runnable unless the owner pauses first; default maxPayout = 0 turns any pause, deploy-wiring delay or idle stretch into one rate x D windfall (confirms CODE-001 as a Low owner footgun, with a corrected safe sequence)
findings.relatesTo: CODE-001 (same root cause; merge, do not double-file)
findings.description: pendingPayout() is uncapped when maxPayout == 0 (the deploy default), and accrual continues through pause. burn() reads the pot at its own execution time. An owner who reacts to a large pot with setMaxPayout(cap) while burns are LIVE can be front-run by any NFT holder, who takes the whole uncapped pot. CORRECTION to CODE-001: 'pausing first does not help' is only half true. While paused, burn() reverts EnforcedPause, so setMaxPayout() and setRatePerDay() are NOT front-runnable. The sequence pause -> setMaxPayout(cap) -> unpause binds the cap on everything accrued during the pause. The only part that escapes is the pot standing at the moment the pause tx lands, which a front-run of pause() can take, and which in a live market with an idle-NFT overhang is small (a few hours of accrual). The real hazard is therefore narrower: (a) an owner who unpauses (or enables the rate before Antimatter.setApprovedMinter / setAuthorizedBurner have landed, which makes burns revert and lets the pot grow) without first setting a cap, which hands rate x D to the first back-runner; (b) an owner who tries to cap a live, un-paused contract.
findings.attackPath: ratePerDay = 25e18 (10x the story example), maxPayout = 0. A pause lasts D = 14 days, so the pot is 350 AM. The owner calls unpause() without setting a cap. A searcher back-runs unpause in the same block with burn(id, 349e18) and receives 350 AM, about $312 at $0.89/AM. Variant: the owner calls setMaxPayout(25e18) un-paused, and a holder front-runs and takes 350 AM. Either way the excess (325 AM, about $290) is minted rather than forfeited.
findings.economicImpact: Bounded by ratePerDay x D. This is the owner's own budgeted emission for the period, so no AM is minted beyond what the configured rate already implied. The loss is only the failure of a forfeiture the owner later intended, as phUSD dilution of (rate x D - cap). Not a theft from users: the winner still burns an NFT.
findings.whyFootgun: Story-053 says maxPayout 'prevents a long idle period from turning into one large mint', but that holds only if the cap was set BEFORE the idle period or while paused. A competent owner who deploys with the default 0 and uses pause as an incident stop could be surprised that unpause dumps the entire paused-period accrual. Law 3: in scope as an operational hazard.
findings.safeConfig: (1) In the phStaging2 deploy story, call setMaxPayout(rate x target interval, e.g. 1-2 days of accrual) BEFORE setRatePerDay(nonzero), and set the rate only after setAuthorizedBurner + setApprovedMinter. (2) To shrink a large pot: pause -> setMaxPayout(cap) [-> setRatePerDay(...)] -> unpause, never setMaxPayout while live. (3) Note that setRatePerDay(0) PRESERVES the pot and does not forfeit it.
findings.evidence: NFTBonfire.sol:117-122 (cap applied at read only when maxPayout != 0), :97 whenNotPaused on burn only, :135-139 setMaxPayout checkpoint (capped at OLD max, so a 0 old max stores the full pot uncapped until the new max applies on read), :149-156 pause does not touch accrual. Story-053 Concerns: 'Pause does not freeze accrual'.
findings.profitability: Free option for any holder of any NFT: cost is 1 NFT (about $0 marginal for idle inventory) plus gas, against a gain of rate x D.
findings.affectedParties: phUSD holders (dilution of rate x D - intended cap)
findings.severityReasoning: Low. Owner-triggered, no user principal at risk, and the impact is bounded by emission the owner already budgeted. A safe operational sequence exists. Not Medium: there is no value outflow beyond the configured rate, and it requires an owner action that the story's text partly warns about ('pause does not freeze accrual').

findings.title: Winner-takes-all sniping: per-interval MEV is about ratePerDay x interval x $0.89; minPayout fully protects a non-attacker's NFT, so no loss beyond what story-053 accepts
findings.description: Any holder can copy a pending burn with their own NFT. The first burn in a block takes the pot, and any later burn in the same block sees 0. The victim either reverts (minPayout > 0, costs gas only, NFT kept) or, with minPayout = 0, burns the NFT for ~0. After a snipe the pot restarts from 0 and accrues per second, so a victim's later tx sees rate x dt, which is far below any minPayout of about pendingPayout - tolerance. There is no partial-fill path that burns the NFT for a fraction of its expected value while minPayout is honestly set.
findings.attackPath: Sizing at rate = 2.5 AM/day: the pot after 6h is 0.625 AM, about $0.56; after 1 day it is 2.5 AM, about $2.23. With about 772 idle NFTs whose marginal value is about 0, bots burn as soon as pot > gas (about 80k gas x 1 gwei x $2,322, about $0.19, which is about 0.085 AM, about 49 minutes of accrual). Expected MEV per event is cents to a few dollars. At 25 AM/day it is about $22/day in total. Victim with minPayout = 0: loses one NFT whose market value is about the clearing pot (about $0-$2 at sane rates); never more than its cheapest replacement ($3.6-$10).
findings.economicImpact: No change to total emission (ECON valuation). Only the identity of the recipient changes. The loss to a minPayout = 0 user is a self-chosen opt-out (story: 'pass 0 to opt out'; C4 known-invalid: user input mistakes).
findings.lawWeighing: Law 2: the story explicitly accepts front-runnability and supplies minPayout as the remedy, so the implementation is faithful. Law 1: no non-attacker loss exists beyond the opt-out, and the protocol loses nothing because emission is time-bounded. The only Law-1-relevant obligation is on the UI follow-up story: it must pass a non-zero minPayout (the story already instructs 'pendingPayout() minus tolerance'). Track as a UI obligation, not a contract finding.
findings.profitability: Profitable for searchers whenever pot > gas, but tiny at story-example rates.
findings.affectedParties: Only users who opt out of minPayout
findings.severityReasoning: No severity. Story-intended, protected by an in-contract slippage floor, and does not grow total emission.

findings.title: Legacy V1 -> V2 mint route is still live (V1 NFTMinter unpaused, NFTMigrator still an authorized V2 minter): fresh V2 claim NFTs can be minted at stale V1 prices (about $3.6) that bypass V2 dispatchers. Inert before story-053, now value-bearing at the bonfire
findings.contract: src/NFTMinterV2.sol (mintFor) via deployed NFTMigrator 0x22c0fc1a / V1 NFTMinter 0xd936461f
findings.description: Story 059 (phStaging2) removed NFTMigrator from mainnet-addresses.ts, but on-chain the migrator still holds authorizedMinters == true on NFTMinterV2 and is still an authorizedBurner on V1, and V1 is unpaused with dispatchers 1/2/3/5/6 enabled. All V1 supply is 0, so this is no longer a migration path for existing holders. It is purely a parallel MINT route. Fork-verified at block 26280445: transfer 1e6 sats of WBTC to a fresh EOA, approve V1, call V1.mint(WBTC, 5, user) (status 1), then NFTMigrator.migrate() (status 1). The result is V2 balanceOf(user, 5) == 1, and the V1 idx5 price rose 17,624 -> 19,738. Payment goes to the V1 dispatchers, not the V2 ones (Uniboost / UniPoolerV2), and does not advance V2 price growth. Pre-story-053 this was economically inert (a V2 NFT had only staking value), and the owner, having retired the migrator from the address book, would be surprised that it can now mint redeemable bonfire tickets.
findings.attackPath: Mint a V1 idx2 NFT for 1.0786 SCX (about $3.68 at SCX $3.42), or a V1 idx1 NFT for 288.28 EYE (about $3.56). Call migrate() to receive a V2 NFT of the same index, then burn it at NFTBonfire for the pot. Cost escalates 10% per mint per index: 10 NFTs on idx2 cost about $58.6, and 30 NFTs about $605.
findings.economicImpact: Bounded and small. It does not raise total bonfire emission (time-bounded), and the about 772 idle V2 NFTs already undercut the V1 route as a burn source. Real effects: (1) it diverts mint revenue away from the live V2 dispatchers; (2) it lowers the cost floor used in the phoenix-nft-staking re-arm calculus (ECON-004) from $10 to about $3.6; (3) it is an unmonitored mint path into a token that is now value-bearing.
findings.safeConfig: NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedMinter(0x22c0fc1aae66873abd029448eaf15a2fd7eed140, false) and/or pause the V1 minter, ideally in the same phStaging2 story that wires NFTBonfire. Verify afterwards that no other authorizedMinters exist (only one AuthorizedMinterSet(true) log on V2 to date).
findings.evidence: On-chain reads plus a fork simulation (commands in the run transcript). NFTMinterV2.sol:206-215 mintFor has no payment and no price update. Historical NFTMigrator source: git show df4d590 (migrate() burns V1 balance and calls v2.mintFor per unit).
findings.profitability: Profitable only if the bonfire pot exceeds about $3.6 and the minter wins the race against idle-inventory holders. With maxPayout below about 4 AM that never happens.
findings.affectedParties: V2 dispatcher revenue (minor); phUSD holders are unaffected beyond the budgeted emission
findings.severityReasoning: Low. A non-obvious deployment-state footgun made relevant by story-053. No emission beyond budget and no user loss, so not Medium. Routed to phStaging2 for the revoke, because the root cause is deployment state, not yield-claim-nft source.

findings.title: Cross-project expired premise: phoenix-nft-staking 858e9e80 (wont-fix) and 521c20ad (open). 'Claim NFT has no realizable redemption value' becomes false once NFTBonfire is wired, but the closure's quantitative margin survives at sane rates. Re-anchor the rationale and add a numeric re-arm trigger
findings.contract: phoenix-nft-staking src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol (gate) <- yield-claim-nft src/NFTBonfire.sol (new redemption path)
findings.rootCauseClass: expired-closure-premise (cross-project; routed note, not a refile)
findings.severity: Informational here. In phoenix-nft-staking: stays wont-fix (858e9e80) / conditional (521c20ad) at sane rates; re-arm to Medium only past the thresholds below
findings.description: The run-21 closure of 858e9e80 rested on the verified premise that NFTMinterV2 has no holder-callable redemption path, so a nudge snatcher's 40 freshly minted NFTs are sunk cost. Once phStaging2 wires NFTBonfire (setAuthorizedBurner + Antimatter.setApprovedMinter + a non-zero rate), each NFT can be burned for one pot. The premise is literally false from then on, and per the expired-closure rule the rationale must be re-anchored. Quantitatively, however, the bonfire's contribution to a snatcher's recovery is bounded by the TOTAL emission they can capture, not by NFT count: over horizon T, recovery_AM <= min(ratePerDay x T, 40 x maxPayout [if set]), and the snatcher competes with about 772 idle plus about 4.6k staked NFTs for that stream.
findings.attackPath: Gate economics on the live index-4 BatchNFTMinter: qualifying cost is about 40 x $18.32 = $733 USDS. The owner reports the nudge pot has never exceeded 50% of qualifying cost, so pot <= about $366. The re-arm requires bonfire recovery >= cost - pot, about $367, which is about 412 AM at $0.89. At rate = 2.5 AM/day, even capturing 100% of emission would take about 165 days, during which the remaining NFT holders burn too, so it is not profitable. Thresholds for re-arm within a 7-day horizon: ratePerDay >= about 59 AM/day AND (maxPayout == 0 OR maxPayout >= about 10.3 AM). For RatchetBatchNFTMinter (idx7, $2,800 cost) the thresholds are about 4x higher. Using ECON-003's $3.6 floor does not change the gate math (the gate pins the dispatcher index; the snatcher must pay V2 prices for the 40 qualifying mints).
findings.economicImpact: None at the story-example rate. If the owner later sets a high rate without a cap, the nudge pot becomes atomically or near-term profitable to farm and the 521c20ad race becomes live. Those harms are dilution plus nudge-pot capture, at Medium in phoenix-nft-staking.
findings.routing: Expired-closure note to phoenix-nft-staking (its own bucket, not a regression). Rewrite the 858e9e80 triageReason off 'no realizable value' onto the quantitative bound above. Add re-arm watch: ratePerDay x 7d x v_AM >= (nudgeSize x price - typical pot) with maxPayout x nudgeSize x v_AM above the same bound. 521c20ad keeps its single shared re-arm watch. Also bear in mind that the frozen mainnet BatchNFTMinter (0x068395..., idx4, nudgeSize 40) has no ledger entry of its own (memory note) and the same arithmetic applies to it.
findings.evidence: Live configs: BatchNFTMinter 0x068395 nudgeSize=40 idx=4; RatchetBatchNFTMinter 0x81896f nudgeSize=40 idx=7; V2 idx4 price 18.317665e18 USDS, idx7 70e6 USDC. NFTBonfire.sol:97-112 (one pot per burn, reset to 0).
findings.severityReasoning: Informational here. The premise text has expired but the economic margin has not: break-even needs a rate about 24x the story example, uncapped. Escalate only if the deploy story picks a rate or cap near the thresholds.
findings.confidence: medium (relies on owner-reported nudge-pot history and the current phUSD price)

findings.title: Bonfire AM must be priced as phUSD dilution, not opportunity cost; ratePerDay is a dilution budget (sizing note for the deploy story)
findings.description: Recorded so that later triage does not suppress bonfire over-emission findings under the 'externally-derived yield = opportunity cost' memory rule. AM is redeemable via permissionless annihilate into unbacked phUSD (about $0.89/AM at phUSD $0.947), so every AM minted dilutes phUSD collateralization. This is intended by story-053 and bounded by ratePerDay x time; the contract is correct. The open item is sizing: rate R costs 365R unbacked phUSD/yr against the current about 97.7k supply (R=2.5 gives 0.93%/yr; R=25 gives 9.3%/yr). There is no supply cap on Antimatter, and the bonfire has no lifetime budget.
findings.severityReasoning: No finding. Guidance for the phStaging2 deploy story and the suppression rules.

refuted.hypothesis: Profitable mint-to-burn loop (mint cost < expected pot)
refuted.result: Not a protocol leak at any rate. Total emission is time-bounded, so a mint-to-burn only adds dispatcher revenue compared with an idle-NFT burn of the same pot. It is profitable to the minter only if the pot exceeds about $3.6 (ECON-003 route) or about $10 (V2 idx3), and about 772 idle NFTs undercut both. Price growth (1-2bp) is a revenue ratchet for the protocol, not a cost.

refuted.hypothesis: Free mint path via authorized minters
refuted.result: The only authorized V2 minter is NFTMigrator. It is not free: it requires a paid V1 mint (ECON-003). BatchNFTMinters pay full V2 price via mint().

refuted.hypothesis: Rate change re-prices elapsed time / setter sandwich
refuted.result: Refuted. Both setters _checkpoint() at the old rate/cap first (NFTBonfire.sol:127-139). A burn front-running a rate decrease receives exactly the checkpointed amount it would have received anyway. The first setRatePerDay from 0 checkpoints a 0 pot, so there is no enable windfall.

refuted.hypothesis: Burn from another holder via NFTMinterV2's approval-less burn
refuted.result: Refuted. burn() hard-codes msg.sender (line 106); a non-holder reverts ERC1155InsufficientBalance (profile-verified).

assumptions: phUSD/sUSDS UniV2 spot (0.947) used for AM value; deeper realisation suffers slippage in a pool of about $23k.
Antimatter exchangeRate taken as about 1e18 for valuation (2p - 1).
PhusdStableMinter maxMintPerDay getter reverted on the live minter 0x94855ACA, so the throttle on annihilate realisation was not confirmed.
Nudge pot <= 50% of qualifying cost per owner statement (memory externally-derived-yield-opportunity-cost-not-loss).
